meanings.note: the present tense is normally left out: я мэр = I am the mayor
Present есть; у меня есть = I have. Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to be; there is'.
future: буду / будешь ... + infinitive

examples.trans: You will be asking for forgiveness.

meanings.note: For emphasis.

examples.trans: I have no idea at all.

examples.text: Я человек чистый. Я вообще не вор.
examples.trans: I'm an honest man. I'm not a thief at all.

meanings.note: 'закрывать глаза на' + accusative = to turn a blind eye to

examples.text: Я не буду закрывать на это глаза.
examples.trans: I'm not going to close my eyes to this.

examples.text: А я глаза на это закрывать не буду. Я подниму людей!
examples.trans: Well, I'm not going to close my eyes to this. I'll rally people!

говорить.gloss: to speak, to say, to talk

meanings.note: Я тебе говорю = I'm telling you. Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to speak, to say, to talk', paired with 'сказать'.
Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to speak, to say, to talk', paired with 'сказать'.

examples.trans: I have a lot to do.

examples.text: Мне некогда об этом думать. Слишком много дел.
examples.trans: I have no time to think about that. There's too much to do.

meanings.note: + genitive.

related.gloss: to reach, walk as far as

meanings.note: A fact or a person.

examples.text: Спасибо, спасибо! Как вы все знаете, я родился и вырос в Синеозерске.
examples.trans: Thank you, thank you! As you all know, I was born and grew up in Sineozersk.

meanings.note: Imperative: извини / извините.
+ accusative (кого).

examples.trans: Sorry, I didn't mean to offend you.

examples.text: Аркадий Борисович, извините, тут к вам человек.
examples.trans: Arkady Borisovich, excuse me, there's someone here to see you.

meanings.note: + dative. Core Russian prep meaning 'to, towards' in everyday speech.

examples.trans: There's someone here to see you.

examples.text: Аркадий Борисович, извините, тут к вам человек.
examples.trans: Arkady Borisovich, I'm sorry, there's a man here to see you.

meanings.note: in the instrumental: 'кем ты работаешь?'

examples.trans: Arkady Borisovich, who are your rivals?

meanings.note: в кухне / на кухне = in the kitchen, на кухню = to the kitchen
E.g. русская кухня. Entered Russian via Polish 'kuchnia' and Middle High German 'küchen', ultimately from Late Latin 'coquina' (from 'coquere', to cook).

examples.trans: And the kitchen is over there.
We are sitting in the kitchen.

examples.text: Проходите, пожалуйста! Как видите, большой коридор, а там кухня.
examples.trans: Come on in, please! As you can see, a big hall, and the kitchen is over there.

meanings.note: + prepositional: на сайте. Core Russian prep meaning 'on, onto; for' in everyday speech.
+ accusative: на второй срок. Core Russian prep meaning 'on, onto; for' in everyday speech.

examples.trans: The programme is on the website.
He is running for a second term.

examples.text: Я очень люблю наш город. Поэтому я иду на второй срок.
examples.trans: I love our town very much. That's why I'm running for a second term.

meanings.en: must, need to, it is necessary
meanings.note: Надо + infinitive.

examples.trans: We need to do even more.

meanings.note: кого + instrumental: назвать меня плохим словом
Prefix 'на-' marks surface contact, accumulation, or completing a quantity (stem 'звать').

examples.trans: You called me a bad word.
What will you name your son?

examples.text: Ты назвал меня плохим словом. Меня, начальника!
examples.trans: You called me a bad word. Me, your boss!

meanings.note: наш, наша, наше, наши; agrees with the noun

examples.text: Я очень люблю наш город. Поэтому я иду на второй срок.
examples.trans: I love our town very much. That's why I'm running for a second term.

meanings.note: goes right before the word it negates
+ prepositional; об before a vowel: об этом

examples.text: Мне некогда об этом думать. Слишком много дел.
examples.trans: I have no time to think about that. There's too much to do.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'to her', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Она нашла нас на новом месте.
examples.trans: She found us at the new place.
That is it, she got really offended.
She is not answering her phone.

meanings.note: A door, a window. Prefix 'от-' ('away from, off') marks separation, completion, or response (stem 'крыть').

examples.trans: Open the door. Is this flat nine?

meanings.note: Informal.
Мой парень = my boyfriend.

examples.text: Всегда мечтала познакомиться с друзьями моего парня.
examples.trans: I've always dreamed of meeting my boyfriend's friends.

meanings.note: Понял? = got it?; понял = got it.

examples.trans: Share it all equally with everyone, understand?

meanings.note: On foot, once. Used as a perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to come, to arrive', paired with 'приходить'.

examples.trans: Security will be here any moment.

examples.text: Не надо, Самсон. Сейчас придёт охрана.
examples.trans: Don't, Samson. Security will be here any second.

meanings.en: to pester, to bother, to harass (+ к + dat.)
meanings.note: Prefix 'при-' indicates approaching, attachment, or slight degree of action (stem 'ставать').

examples.text: Не приставай ко мне с вопросами!
Они приставали к Нине. Нина, ну расскажите вы ему!
examples.trans: They were pestering Nina. Nina, come on, tell him!

meanings.note: + instrumental; со before some consonant clusters: со всеми

examples.trans: Share it all equally with everyone, understand?

meanings.note: forms the superlative: самый главный = the most important
Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('the most; the very').

examples.trans: The most important thing is the people.
Do you know the main thing?

meanings.note: Literally 'until the meeting'.
'сейчас буду' = I'll be right there

examples.text: Конечно, помогу. Кто у вас сейчас начальник?
examples.trans: Of course I'll help. Who's your boss now?

meanings.note: а вы случайно не...? = are you by any chance...?

examples.trans: Are you by any chance Samson?

examples.text: Здравствуйте! Извините, а вы случайно не Самсон?
examples.trans: Hello! Excuse me, are you by any chance Samson?

meanings.note: + accusative.
the imperative 'слушай' starts a sentence, like 'look, ...'
'Слушаю' = I'm listening.

examples.text: Слушай, Самсон, я тут подумал. Твой начальник — такой опытный специалист.
examples.trans: Listen, Samson, I've been thinking. Your boss is such an experienced specialist.

points at something: это моё = that's mine
Linking word: главное — это народ. Core Russian pron meaning 'this, that; it is' in everyday speech.
